record.title: incident retro for the phishing wave from last week
record.summary: The team reviewed the phishing wave from last week. The timeline showed a 38-minute gap between the first reported click (09:14) and the first containment action (09:52), with 11 minutes of that delay attributed to Marcus being in a meeting. Marcus committed to drafting a documented escalation runbook to avoid routing through a single person, with a deadline of 2026-08-09. Scope analysis revealed 214 users received the email, 9 clicked, and 3 entered credentials; all three reset within the hour, and no successful logins occurred from attacker infrastructure. Rio noted that the credential entries were on a fake ADFS page and highlighted that the finance group still lacks phishing-resistant MFA due to an exemption from the ERP migration that has persisted for two years. Dana confirmed that removing the exemption is not disruptive since the ERP vendor now supports FIDO keys. Rio owns removing the exemption, planning to pilot with five finance users next week before rolling out to the rest of the group. Priya confirmed that phishing domains were added to the blocklist feed and a takedown request was sent to the registrar an hour ago. Regarding detection, the fake page was live for six hours before the first report; Dana assigned adding a canary token to the login footer template as finding three but placed it in the backlog without an owner. Marcus noted that users who reported received no acknowledgment, causing two to re-report; Dana also placed the auto-acknowledgment feature in the backlog.
